investigation_summary: Reconciliation of candidate recall measurements across validation pipeline and unconstrained full-corpus benchmarks.

measurements.target_pool_size: ~400,000 targets per country (Needed GT matches for 115k S1 + 300,000 background pool)
measurements.definition: Percentage of validation S1 true matches retrieved in top-25 candidate sets when querying the training target pool.
measurements.notes: Target pool is conditioned on training S1 entities plus a 300k background pool.

measurements.target_pool_size: 6,186,873 US target records and 4,133,346 India target records (All S2 + S3 records)
measurements.definition: Percentage of true matches captured when querying against the entire unconstrained 6.18M target pool.
measurements.notes: The hard frequency pruning threshold of 2,500 represents only 0.04% of a 6.18M dataset, causing severe candidate drops on common industry words. Soft-IDF solves this by replacing binary pruning with continuous entropy weighting log(N / (df+1)), boosting recall by +16.26%.

conclusion: The discrepancy is entirely explained by target pool size (400k sample vs 6.18M full corpus) and the aggressive 0.04% hard-prune threshold. Soft-IDF successfully eliminates the hard-prune drop on large corpora.
